fx.fix.title: Batch fix
fx.fix.confirm: A new conversation will fix the {{count}} selected issue(s) using the built-in workflow. The fix conversation never runs Git write commands.
fx.fix.stageNotice: Auto-staging is on: when the whole automation chain finishes (after verification when it is enabled, otherwise right after the last fix batch), the plugin runs git add on the files declared in this run's fix results. Those files are staged in full, so edits that already existed before the fix are staged too; the toast says so. Files declared only by "not found" results are not staged; files declared only by "pending" results stay candidates and are counted separately in the toast. Never git add -A, never commit.
fx.fix.step1: Verify each issue against the code before editing
fx.fix.step2: Parallel read-only investigation with affected-file lists
fx.fix.step3: Conflict analysis: overlapping files go serial, the rest in parallel
fx.fix.tooMany: {{count}} issues selected; at most {{limit}} per run is recommended.

fx.cleanup.confirmDeleteAll: Delete all {{count}} issue(s) and {{sessions}} conversation(s)? Deletion cannot be undone, and the source links of deleted conversations are cleared too.
fx.cleanup.allRunningHint: A conversation is still running or may still be running. Archive all / Delete all also handles conversations, so wait for it to finish and retry.
fx.cleanup.allRiskHint: The run state of historical conversations cannot be confirmed. Tick the risk confirmation below before handling everything.
fx.cleanup.fixedHint: Fixed issues are pre-selected; not-found, fixing, and open issues must be selected explicitly. Archive all / Delete all handles every unarchived issue and all conversations with the same action.
fx.cleanup.deleteWarn: Deleting issues and conversations cannot be undone.
fx.cleanup.runningBlocked: The conversation is still running; cleanup was cancelled. Wait for it to finish or stop tracking first.
fx.cleanup.runningHint: This conversation is still running and cannot be archived or deleted.
fx.cleanup.detachedHint: Tracking is stopped, but the conversation may still be running; deleting it loses later messages.
fx.cleanup.historicalHint: Historical conversations are not tracked; their run state cannot be confirmed. Archive is recoverable, delete is not.
fx.cleanup.riskAck: I confirm these conversations have finished and want to continue
fx.cleanup.unverifiedBlocked: A conversation's run state could not be verified, so cleanup was cancelled. Confirm it has finished and retry.

fx.settings.title: Settings
fx.settings.reviewModeHint: Default opens the scope picker; Staged changes or Working tree changes start the review immediately. When that scope has no changes, the scope picker opens instead.
fx.settings.parallelHint: The parallel limit is written into the fix prompt to cap parallel investigation and implementation in one run. It does not change host concurrency; work beyond the limit is queued.
fx.settings.apiProfileHint: Pick the API profile used by review / fix / verification conversations. Follow global settings uses the host's active profile. Changes affect conversations created afterwards.
fx.settings.apiProfilesEmpty: No API profiles in the host yet; create one in global settings first.
fx.settings.apiProfilesFailed: Failed to load the API profile list; save other settings and retry.
fx.settings.apiProfileMissing: Saved profile "{{name}}" is not in the current list (it may have been deleted or renamed). Switch to Follow global settings and save; otherwise every new conversation retries it first.
fx.settings.severityScopeHint: Only the selected severities are written into the issue list after a review. Minor is off by default; clearing everything restores the default scope (Critical + Major).
fx.settings.readFailed: Settings could not be read. This change applies to the current session only and was not written to local storage. Check local storage and retry.
fx.settings.loadFailedNotice: Settings could not be read, so defaults are shown. Saving writes only the items you changed; untouched items keep their stored values.
fx.settings.autoFixHint: On by default. The first automatic fix asks for confirmation; after that, only issues added or reopened by this review are fixed automatically. When settings cannot be read, a confirmation is required first.
fx.settings.autoCleanup: Clean up automatically after all fixes finish
fx.settings.autoCleanupHint: After every batch finishes, handle this run's fixed issues plus the conversation types selected below. Not-found issues are never cleaned automatically; review them in Handle results first.
fx.settings.autoCleanupSessionsHint: Only this run's conversations covered by the auto-cleanup action are handled. Unchecked types are kept and can be cleaned in Handle results. Fix and verification conversations are selected by default; review conversations are kept. When review conversations are selected, a review conversation is cleaned only if every issue it reported is already fixed; conversations still referenced by not-found, open, fixing, or verification-rejected issues are kept so their source links and evidence stay available. Clearing all options cleans issues only.
fx.fix.batchHint: {{count}} issues will run in {{batches}} batches of at most {{limit}}; each batch starts a new conversation after the previous one finishes.

fx.verify.confirm: A read-only conversation will be created and the prompt sent automatically to verify the {{count}} selected fixed issue(s) in {{batches}} batch(es). Verification consumes model calls but does not modify code.

fx.prompts.title: Custom prompts
fx.prompts.description: The fixed rules of all three prompts stay read-only. Additional requirements below are injected into the matching prompt when enabled; empty text or a disabled slot keeps the default behavior.
fx.prompts.slotHint.review: When enabled, appended after the fixed review rules and applied to every review.
fx.prompts.slotHint.fix: When enabled, appended after the hard constraints and applied to every fix batch.
fx.prompts.slotHint.verify: When enabled, appended after the verification method and applied to every verification batch.
fx.prompts.placeholder.review: e.g. Focus on null references and error handling; ignore style-only findings.
fx.prompts.placeholder.fix: e.g. Run pnpm test after changes; do not touch the src/legacy directory.
fx.prompts.placeholder.verify: e.g. Check that type definitions and docs were updated together.
fx.prompts.conflictNote: Additional requirements are supplementary focus and workflow preferences only. Where they conflict with the read-only constraints, safety rules, or the structured output contract, the plugin fixed rules win.
fx.verify.confirmRecheck: A read-only conversation will be created and the prompt sent automatically to re-check the {{count}} selected "not found" issue(s) in {{batches}} batch(es): confirm they are still absent, or overturn the earlier verdict and return them to Open. This consumes model calls but does not modify code.
fx.verify.confirmMixed: A read-only conversation will be created and the prompt sent automatically to re-check the {{count}} selected issue(s) ({{fixed}} fixed, {{notFound}} not found) in {{batches}} batch(es). This consumes model calls but does not modify code.
fx.toast.recheckDone: Re-check finished: {{confirmed}} confirmed absent, {{still}} earlier verdicts overturned and returned to Open, {{uncertain}} need confirmation.
fx.toast.mixedDone: Mixed re-check finished: {{confirmed}} earlier conclusions upheld, {{still}} earlier conclusions overturned and returned to Open, {{uncertain}} need confirmation.
fx.settings.stageAfterFix: Stage changes automatically after all fixes
fx.settings.stageAfterFixHint: Off by default. When the whole automation chain finishes (after verification when it is enabled; a verification error, stopped tracking, a closed verification card, or a timeout also stages at that interruption; otherwise right after the last fix batch), the plugin runs git add on the files declared in this run's fix results. No start-time content baseline is captured, so the start stage runs no Git commands at all; each file is therefore staged in full and edits that already existed before the fix are staged too. Candidates are narrowed by fix conclusion first: files declared only by "not found" results are not staged, while files declared only by "pending" results stay candidates and are counted separately in the toast. When the Git status cannot be read or candidates cannot be confirmed, no git add is run and the candidates are listed instead. A staging failure does not block cleanup; the reason is reported in a toast.

fx.toast.stageUnconfirmed: Auto-stage skipped: none of the candidate files could be confirmed as changed in this run (they may be unchanged, ignored, or use a different path base). Candidates: {{files}}.{{filtered}}
fx.toast.stagePathRejected: Auto-stage skipped: {{count}} candidate path(s) contain characters that cannot be passed to git safely, so no git add was run. Candidates: {{files}}.
fx.toast.stageStatusUnavailable: Auto-stage skipped: could not read the current Git status ({{error}}).
fx.toast.stageNotFoundSkipped: Auto-stage skipped: every candidate file was declared only by "not found" results (those records normally mean no code change). Candidates: {{files}}.
fx.stage.description: Stage this run's fix changes (git add)
fx.stage.pathFiltered: {{count}} more candidate path(s) contain characters that cannot be passed to git safely and were not staged automatically.
fx.stage.repoPathFiltered: {{count}} other changed path(s) in the repository cannot be passed to git safely; they are unrelated to this run and were skipped.
fx.stage.blockedNotice: {{count}} other candidate file(s) declared only by "pending" results were not staged this run (they may be unchanged or use a different path base): {{files}}. Stage them manually in the terminal if they were in fact edited.
fx.stage.blockedStaged: Of these, {{files}} were declared only by "pending" results and were staged in full (paths are relative to the repository root), so edits those files already had are staged too; run git restore --staged if you do not want them staged.
fx.stage.notFoundSkipped: {{count}} more file(s) were declared only by "not found" results and were not staged (those records normally mean no code change); stage them manually in the terminal if they were in fact edited.
fx.stage.wholeFileNotice: These files are staged in full and may include changes that existed before the fix.
fx.stage.sshUnsupported: Auto-staging is not supported for SSH projects; run git add in the remote repository instead.
